text:
marina: Heads-up — I sketched an activation state machine for on‑prem package activation in air‑gapped clusters. Want quick feedback on resume/idempotency guarantees.
aj: Nice. Can you paste the state diagram?
sylvia: @marina can we ensure node reboots don't leave things half-activated? :thinking:
marina: absolutely — idea is to make each activation step idempotent and persist a resume token in the local verifier store. rough states: `downloaded -> verified -> staged -> activating -> activated -> committed` and a `failed` sink.
rene: how do you handle partially applied components (e.g., service A applied, B not)? rollback or continue?
marina: two options: 1) component-level compensating rollback; 2) transactional commit stage where we switch a pointer once all pieces report `activated`. leaning toward #2 for safety but with a limited time window and operator opt-in for auto-rollback.
aj: if we do pointer-swap commit, operators will ask how to inspect progress. need strong observability + small checkpoints.
marina: agreed — plan: each component writes a local checkpoint with `op_id`, `component_id`, `state`, `last_seq`. The controller polls and constructs a view. sample checkpoint record (on node):
```
op_id: pkg-2026-03-09-0723
component: blob-store
state: staged
seq: 42
resume_token: rtoken-ab12
```
ops: Who owns pruning of stale resume tokens? we could leak if upgrades abort often.
marina: we garbage collect tokens after a package reaches `committed` or after operator TTL. tokens also include cryptographic nonce so replays are detectable.
sylvia: What about idempotency for `apply` commands? If the operator retries, we should make server side checks based on `op_id`+`seq`.
marina: exactly. server applies a component only if `seq` > recorded seq for that component, otherwise it's a no-op. That keeps `apply` idempotent.
deploy-bot: new:release pkg-2026-03-09-0723 created by marina :rocket:
rene: edge-case: what if node loses verifier store (disk corrupt) mid-op? do we force a full re-download and verification?
marina: we fallback to full re-verify. but to speed recovery we snapshot proof artifacts in a separate signed store that can be pulled from the operator node via secure USB or ephemeral transfer in airgap flows.
aj: sounds good. can we add a small state for `orphaned` where operator intervention is required before commit?
marina: yep — `orphaned` -> blocks commit and surfaces in console with suggested remediation (re-verify or rebootstrap).
sylvia: docs note: make sure the console exposes `op_id`, `resume_token`, per-component seqs for debugging.
marina: will add a short RFC section on operator UX and a toy CLI: `rwdctl pkg resume --op pkg-2026-03-09-0723 --node node-7`
ops: any perf concerns for polling? thousands of nodes -> we should use push/webhook for node state instead of heavy polling.
marina: agree, push by default, poll fallback. also batch state updates to avoid chattiness.
rene: thanks — this clears up the semantics. i'll sketch the rollback playbook and share later. :+1:
marina: awesome, thanks all. i'll drop the draft RFC in the arch RFCs folder this afternoon and ping again.
